title: Glitch-Free Programmable Divider
constraints: `clk_out` divides `clk` by R = 2·(div + 1), i.e. 2, 4, 6 or 8, with a 50 % duty cycle: high for R/2 cycles, then low for R/2 cycles. It comes straight from a flop.

`div` may change at any time, but a new ratio takes effect **only at the start of an output period** (the edge where `clk_out` rises), and it is used for that whole period (high and low halves). So no high or low phase is ever truncated.
Synchronous reset: `clk_out = 0`, counter 0, and the ratio is loaded from `div`. The first rising edge of `clk_out` comes at the end of the first low half after reset.
hints: State: `q`, a half-period counter `cnt`, and the active half-period `h` (1 … 4).
Each edge: if `cnt == h - 1`, then `cnt <= 0`, `q <= ~q`, and if `q` is about to rise (`q == 0`), load `h <= div + 1`. Otherwise `cnt <= cnt + 1`.
This is how DVFS clock generators change frequency without upsetting the downstream logic.

examples.check: ratio changes only at period boundaries
examples.title: switch
examples.expected: the current period finishes with the old ratio
